item.title: Storms expected on both coasts threatens Thanksgiving travel
item.description: The mayor of San Francisco is asking people in the city not to travel unless "absolutely essential." Meanwhile, a storm moving up the Eastern seaboard could also cause travel delays ahead of Thanksgiving.

item.title: This year's U.N. climate conference was bigger than ever—but did it make progress?
item.description: This year's U.N. climate conference was bigger than ever. But that doesn't necessarily mean there was progress.

item.description: Delegates from nearly 200 countries have been meeting for two weeks to discuss steps to limit global warming.

item.title: Rising seas have forced this Quinault village to relocate
item.description: The Quinault Indian Nation has moved its largest village away from rising seas and tsunamis

item.title: Trump's impact on an Ohio steel plant
item.description: The giant steel plant in Middletown, Ohio planned to switch away from using coke, a refined form of coal. The switch would have cut hazardous air pollution -- and greenhouse gas emissions. But that plan has changed under President Trump

item.title: Senate passes bipartisan energy bill amid environmental concerns
item.description: As Americans struggle with rising energy costs and increased demand driven by AI, the Senate passed a bipartisan bill that will speed up the approval process for data centers and power plants.

item.title: China's emissions have plateaued — and may even be falling
item.description: China and the U.S. are the world's two largest emitters of planet-heating pollution. But experts say China's emissions are now plateauing.
item.content:encoded: China and the U.S. are the world's two largest emitters of planet-heating pollution. But experts say China's emissions are now plateauing.

item.title: China and the U.S. are the world's biggest polluters. And the U.S. is falling behind
item.description: The two largest emitters of greenhouse gases are China and the United States. Now, the countries' stories are diverging: many Chinese provinces are reducing coal use, while the U.S. is falling behind on climate technologies.
item.content:encoded:
The two largest emitters of greenhouse gases are China and the United States. Now, the countries' stories are diverging: many Chinese provinces are reducing coal use, while the U.S. is falling behind on climate technologies.

item.title: They tried to torture him into leaving Iraq. He refused to abandon the nature he protects
item.description: Iran-backed militias kidnapped and tortured him, but Jassim al-Asadi is still on a mission to save Iraq's marshes, and a way of life stretching back to the dawn of history.

item.title: What influence does the U.S. have at this year's U.N. climate talks?
item.description: The U.S. isn't at the negotiating table at the UN climate conference but attendees are talking about the midterms. Democratic members Congress are vowing to undo actions by the Trump administration.
